nodes.name: Heterogeneous curvature lignin spheres self-assembly
nodes.procedure: Typically, 10 mg of KLE and 6 mg BHT were first dissolved into THF in 1.0 mg mL-1. Then, four times the volume of deionized water was dropped into the above solution via a peristaltic pump at a rate of 8 mL min-1. With the complete volatilization of THF, the suspension of lignin spheres with continuous heterogeneous curvature was obtained.

nodes.name: HeterC-LCS Ru adsorption hydrothermal treatment
nodes.procedure: 0.0068 mmol ruthenium acetate was added to the above suspension [lignin spheres with heterogeneous curvature] to absorb for 30 min. Then the suspension was hydrothermal reaction for 2 h at 160°C in an autoclave. Subsequently, a dark brown powder was obtained via cooling, centrifuging, and freeze-drying.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH (three-electrode setup)
nodes.source_text: The HER performance of the HeterC-LCS and reference samples was measured in a 1M KOH electrolyte via a CHI660e electrochemical workstation. The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) plots in Figure 3A displayed that the HeterC-LCS reached a very low overpotential of 9.2 mV versus RHE at 10 mA cm⁻²... mass activity ... 72.8 A mg⁻¹ and price activity ... 6999.5 A dollar⁻¹ at an overpotential of 100 mV ... TOF of 38.1 H₂ s⁻¹ at 100 mV ... stable for over 600 h at 1 A cm⁻².

nodes.name: HeterC-LCS
aliases: continuous heterogeneous-curvature Ru single-atom/lignin carbon nanoreactors

nodes.evidence_snippet: A monodisperse HeterC-LCS was probed using the SEM and TEM (Figure 1B,C).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals curvature difference at the bottom and open hole of HeterC-LCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to profile structures in Figure 1C, the HeterC-LCS showed the curvature difference at the bottom and the open hole.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM shows Ru single-atoms with diameter of bright dots about 1.4 Å in HeterC-LCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) listed in Figure 1D showed that the Ru single-atom was located in the HeterC-LCS.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows uniform distribution of C, N, O, S, and Ru elements in HeterC-LCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S3 (Supporting Information), all elements, including C, N, O, S, and Ru, were uniformly distributed in HeterC-LCS.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows two wide peaks at 23° and 44° for (002) and (100) planes of carbon matrix with no observable Ru characteristic peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two wide peaks were exhibited at about 23° and 44° in the XRD spectrum, indicating the (002) and (100) planes of the carbon matrix (Figure 2A).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows ID/IG = 0.92 for HeterC-LCS indicating more defect sites than HomoC-LCS (ID/IG = 0.94); no crystalline Ru nanoparticle signal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The intensity ratio (ID/IG) for D and G bands indicated that HeterC-LCS (ID/IG = 0.92) possessed more defect sites than that of HomoC-LCS (ID/IG = 0.94).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Ru 3p XPS shows Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2 peaks indicating Ru^{n+} from Ru-N coordination with slight positive shift for HeterC-LCS; N 1s shows five peaks: pyridinic N (N6), Ru-N, pyrrolic N (N5), graphitic N, oxidized N (N-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S11 (Supporting Information) shows that the HeterC-LCS and HomoC-LCS presented the C, N, O, S, and Ru elements. Among, the high-resolution Ru 3p spectra (Figure 2C) of each sample could be deconvoluted into two peaks: Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2, meaning that the composition of Ru is Ru^{n+}. Thereinto, the Ru^{n+} can be assigned to the Ru-N coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES absorption edge between Ru foil (Ru0) and RuO2 (Ru4+) indicates average positive valence; HeterC-LCS white line shifts to higher energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2D, the absorption edge of HeterC-LCS and HomoC-LCS was located between the Ru foil (Ru0) and RuO2 (Ru4+) which means that the Ru species in HeterC-LCS and HomoC-LCS exhibited an average positive valence.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT EXAFS shows prominent peak at 1.5 Å for Ru-N/O coordination; no Ru-Ru signal confirming single atom dispersion; Ru-N bond distance 2.07±0.01 Å (HeterC-LCS) and 2.02±0.01 Å (HomoC-LCS); coordination number 4.2±0.2 (HeterC-LCS) and 4.0±0.3 (HomoC-LCS).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform (FT) EXAFS of HeterC-LCS presented a prominent peak at about 1.5 Å (Figure 2E), close to the Ru-O (about 1.4 Å), which can be attributed to the presence of N-coordinated Ru.

properties.technique: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure Fourier Transform

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM shows HeterC-LCS exhibits significant potential change at edge and gaps while HomoC-LCS shows homogeneous potential (630 mV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to Figure 4C-E, HomoC-LCS possessed a relatively homogenous potential (630 mV) around the spheres, while the HeterC-LCS exhibited a significant potential change at its edge and gaps.

nodes.characterization_summary: SHINERS shows Stark tuning rate of 97.8 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹ for HeterC-LCS vs 43.2 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹ for HomoC-LCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For HeterC-LCS, the stark tuning rate is 97.8 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹, which shows a significant increase over the HomoC-LCS (43.2 cm⁻¹ V⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS demonstrates excellent HER kinetics for HeterC-LCS; phase peak angles decrease with potential and are consistently lower than HomoC-LCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The excellent HER reaction kinetics of HeterC-LCS were also demonstrated by the electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), as depicted in Figures S16-S18 (Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of HeterC-LCS after durability test shows no obvious Ru single-atom agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inset in (G) is the HR-TEM image of HeterC-LCS after the durability test.
